title: Hatching and Freezing Gemmules from the Freshwater Sponge Ephydatia muelleri
author: Sally P Leys
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.863hzgn
materials: Ungemach LF, Souza K, Fell PE, Loomis SH.

steps.title: Prepare tools and chill reagents
steps.instruction: Label 20–50 cryovials and a storage box; pre‑chill the box in the –80 °C freezer. Pre‑chill high‑quality distilled water to 3 °C. Assemble the 50 mL Falcon tube with cord‑uroy tied to the cap and a 15 mm Petri dish with cord‑uroy glued inside. Wet the cord‑uroy on both tube and dish with ice‑cold distilled water.

steps.title: Free gemmules from skeleton
steps.instruction: Place the skeleton containing gemmules into cold distilled water on ice. Using sterile wide‑tipped forceps (or the cord‑uroy tools), gently rub the skeleton between the cord‑uroy‑lined Falcon tube and the Petri dish to roll the gemmules off the skeleton without applying excessive pressure. For tightly embedded gemmules, dissect under a compound microscope on ice with sterile teasing needles or fine forceps, discarding non‑viable gemmules.

steps.title: Transfer gemmules to ice‑cold water
steps.instruction: Squeeze ice‑cold distilled water onto the cord‑uroy‑lined Petri dish until the freed gemmules fall into a deeper glass bowl filled with ice‑cold distilled water; keep the bowl on ice for the remainder of the procedure.

steps.title: Sort gemmules and remove debris
steps.instruction: Use a pipette attached to a suction hose to draw off loose spicules and debris while swirling the bowl. Add fresh ice‑cold water with a squirt bottle to one side; healthy gemmules sink to the bottom centre, dead husks and debris rise to the surface. Repeat until only healthy gemmules remain. If suction is too aggressive, use a wide‑bore pipette to pick individual gemmules and transfer them to a new Petri dish with ice‑cold water.

steps.title: Sterilize gemmules with H2O2
steps.instruction: Remove excess distilled water from the dish, add 1 % H₂O₂, and shake gently for 5 min at 4 °C. Floating dead or damaged gemmules pop and can be poured off. Quickly add ice‑cold distilled water and rinse the healthy gemmules 4–5 times with gentle washes to eliminate all H₂O₂. Place the rinsed gemmules in a new sterile Petri dish with ice‑cold water, seal with parafilm, and keep at 3 °C in an incubator until needed (several weeks for vernalization).

steps.title: Prepare 20% DMSO cryoprotectant
steps.instruction: Mix 40 mL cold 1× M‑medium (or 1× Strekal’s medium) with 10 mL sterile DMSO to obtain a 20 % DMSO solution. Store the solution in the refrigerator until it reaches 3 °C; ensure it remains cold before use.

steps.title: Mix gemmules with cryoprotectant
steps.instruction: Using a wide‑bore pipette, transfer 15–20 gemmules into a 2 mL cryovial. Add 750 mL cold 1× M‑medium (or 1× Strekal’s medium) then immediately add 750 mL pre‑chilled 20 % DMSO, yielding a final 10 % DMSO concentration. Gently invert the cryovial 4–5 times to mix, keeping the suspension ice‑cold.

steps.title: Incubate mixture on ice
steps.instruction: Keep the cryovials on ice for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Freeze gemmules at –80°C
steps.instruction: Place the cryovials into a box and transfer the box to a –80 °C freezer. Leave undisturbed to freeze; frozen gemmules can be stored at –80 °C for months.

steps.title: Thaw gemmules on ice
steps.instruction: Remove cryovials from the –80 °C freezer and place directly onto ice. Allow the gemmules to thaw completely on ice (≈ 1 hour or longer).

steps.title: Rinse thawed gemmules (H2O2 step)
steps.instruction: Immediately after thawing, repeat the hydrogen‑peroxide sterilization: add 1 % H₂O₂, shake 5 min at 4 °C, discard floating debris, and rinse 4–5 times with ice‑cold distilled water. Keep the rinsed gemmules in distilled water on ice.

steps.title: Remove DMSO by washing
steps.instruction: Using a sterile Pasteur pipette, remove the 10 % DMSO solution from each cryovial and replace it with cold distilled water. Gently invert to mix. Place the cryovials back onto ice and set on a shaker at gentle speed for 5 minutes. Repeat this washing step five times to eliminate residual DMSO.

steps.title: Plate gemmules for hatching
steps.instruction: Option A – Lawn: place gemmules directly into a Petri dish containing M‑medium or Strekal’s medium, cover with tin foil, keep dark at 18–24 °C for 1–2 days until hatching. Option B – Coverslips: soak 15 mm coverslips in 95 % ethanol, flame‑sterilize, place into a sterile Petri dish, add M‑medium or Strekal’s medium, press coverslips down to remove bubbles, and using a wide‑bore pipette place 3–4 gemmules onto each coverslip. Incubate in the dark at 18–24 °C for 1–2 days. After hatching, change medium every 48 hours, never removing all medium or exposing sponges to air.

steps.title: Maintain and feed sponges (optional)
steps.instruction: Add two drops of Liquifry No. 1 to 200 mL of Strekal’s medium or filtered pond water; add ≈ 2 mL of this mixture to each culture dish daily. Liquifry No. 1 contains dextrin, pea flour, egg whites, oil, yeast, and a sulfur‑based preservative.
